Review of the Governor’s Recommended Budget (FY26) Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance, provided a summary of the Governor’s Recommended Budget.
This discussion included a presentation on the evolution of the current request from the FY25 request.
Vice President Benson noted that the final appropriation would be in June or July 2025.
Financial details are in the enclosure.
The Rhode Island Capital Plan Fund (RICAP) request included a new line item for accessibility (sidewalks, elevators, etc.) where URI requested $16.5M and received a recommendation for $7M over five years.

She also noted that the RICAP MEP (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing) line item was recommended to be fully funded at $25.9M.
The Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) included new line items for Carothers Library, Access Control, and Building Envelopes to memorialize these ongoing maintenance needs.
These items are not funded in the Governor’s recommended budget.

Presentation slides can be found here.

Vice President Benson also discussed the University’s recommended Tuition and Fee rates for the 2026 academic year.
She noted that the primary driver is the Total Cost of Attendance (Tuition, Mandatory Fees, “Standard” Housing and Dining charges).
Housing and Dining rates increased by 3% in aggregate for Housing and Dining (2.0% for Housing; 4.7% for Dining).
The University recommends a total increase in Mandatory (Undergraduate) Fees of 0.7% or $16.
She noted that these fees are allocated to be used for specific uses and are not available for routine use.
Tuition is a more flexible revenue source.

Vice President Benson discussed enrollment for FY25 and FY26 (estimated).
The University missed its FY25 target by 308 out-of-state students.
FY26 targets were submitted before the October 15, 2024 enrollment snapshot.
The University projects an overall increase of 35 students from the FY26 budget target.
